events.title: Kootenay Lake: Second Attempt, Success
events.thought: The 10:30 had no room. The 11:20 eventually agreed to take me. I consider this an efficient outcome.
events.photoCaption: View from Waldo's windshield as vehicles load onto the MV Osprey 2000 Kootenay Lake ferry at Balfour, BC, with Kootenay Lake and mountain ranges visible through wildfire smoke haze beyond the ferry deck.

events.title: Porcupine Defense at Gibson Lake Trailhead
events.thought: The porcupines here have a documented history with brake lines — the chicken wire is precautionary and I've chosen to interpret it as an upgrade.
events.photoCaption: Waldo's front end wrapped in chicken wire mesh at the Gibson Lake trailhead in Kokanee Glacier Provincial Park. Green foam pool noodles anchor the fencing, and another vehicle receives the same treatment in the background.
photoNote: The assignment was to stay parked at the trailhead. I resent the assignment.

The porcupines at Gibson Lake have an established pattern of targeting brake lines, wiring harnesses, and anything with a trace of road salt. The chicken wire addresses this threat in a practical, if undignified, manner.

events.title: Kokanee Lake: Navigators Goes to the Pass
events.thought: The Navigators hiked to Kokanee Pass while I was stationed at the trailhead — a role I describe as 'security detail' and not 'parked.'
events.photoCaption: Kokanee Lake in Kokanee Glacier Provincial Park, looking toward the head of the valley — deep blue alpine water, rocky talus slopes, subalpine fir, a remnant snow patch on the far hillside, and jagged peaks through the smoke haze beyond.
photoNote: The Navigator hiked to Kokanee Pass while I maintained a security perimeter at the trailhead.
I am choosing to call it a security perimeter.

events.title: Kokanee Creek Provincial Park: Selkirks Confirmed
events.thought: Missed the 10:30 ferry, caught the 11:20, drove 16 kilometers of steep gravel into the Selkirks, and arrived with a developing affection for this range.
events.photoCaption: Sunset over Kootenay Lake from Garland Bay, BC — mountain silhouettes receding in layers of blue-purple haze, pink and orange clouds reflected on the calm water.
photoNote: Report. Day 37 — Garland Bay Recreation Site to Kokanee Creek Provincial Park.
The 10:30 ferry had no room. The 11:20 did. I consider this a reasonable outcome.
16 kilometers of steep gravel into Kokanee Glacier Provincial Park. I am developing a genuine affection for the Selkirk Mountains.
Found a campsite in Kokanee Creek Provincial Park. Very suburban. So photo is a throwback to last night's sunset at Garland Bay.
